modal-dialog.modal-heading: What if I want to apply part of this year’s federal refund to my estimated federal taxes?

modal-content.p: When your total payments were more than the federal tax you owed, you can choose to:

ul.li: Apply all or part of your overpayment to the next year’s estimated federal taxes

modal-content.p: However, Direct File doesn’t yet support the ability to apply your overpayment to your estimated federal taxes.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What if I want to split my federal refund across multiple accounts?

modal-content.p: It’s possible for taxpayers to split their federal refund and deposit the funds into up to 3 different accounts with U.S. financial institutions. However, Direct File doesn’t support the forms needed to do this yet.

If you don’t have checks, call your bank or see if it’s available when you sign in to your online banking account.

div.h2: We changed your payment method choice.
div.p: You said you wanted to schedule a payment or an Electronic Funds Withdrawal from a bank account. You can’t schedule a withdrawal if you’re filing a paper tax return.
You will have several options to pay when you file a paper return.

div.h2: You’re filing a paper tax return. Here are your options to pay.

fg-alert.heading: You can file your federal taxes only as a paper tax return.

p.strong: You can file your federal taxes only as a paper tax return.

fg-detail.p: You can file your taxes only as a paper tax return because you’re missing an Identity Protection PIN (IP PIN).
Paper returns can take up to 6 weeks to process.
You need an IP PIN to confirm your identity. If you have an IP PIN but can’t find it, you won’t be able to file your tax return electronically.
Try following these instructions to get your IP PIN. Once you have the IP PIN you’re looking for, add it to Direct File.
If you need assistance, chat with customer support.

fg-alert.heading: You can file your federal taxes only as a paper tax return

p.strong: You can file your federal taxes only as a paper tax return because you’re missing last year’s Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) or Self-Select PIN.

fg-detail.p: Paper returns can take up to 6 weeks to process.
Your AGI or Self-Select PIN from last year’s federal tax return is needed to confirm your identity. If you can’t find either, you won’t be able to file your tax return electronically.
Try following these instructions to retrieve your AGI. Or you may continue to file by paper. If you need assistance, chat with customer support.

div.h2: How do you want to pay your federal tax balance?

fg-set.question: How do you want to pay your federal tax balance?

input.option: Schedule payment (Electronic Funds Withdrawal from a bank account)
Pay after I file (for example, check, credit or debit card, IRS payment plan)

modal-content.p: Electronic Funds Withdrawal (EFW) is an e-file/e-pay option offered only when filing your federal taxes using tax preparation software or through a tax professional. Using this payment option, you can pay directly from your bank account.
IRS doesn’t charge a fee to use EFW, but check with your financial institution about any fees it may charge.
Learn about EFW, including what to do if you need to cancel your payment.
